festivals.description: Kajari Teej: women fast and worship Shiva and Parvati for their husband's wellbeing; sing kajari folk songs.

festivals.name: Kalashtami
festivals.description: Kalashtami: Krishna Ashtami of Kala Bhairava, the fierce guardian form of Shiva. Worship at night with a mustard-oil diya and chant Om Namah Shivaya.

festivals.name: Krishna Janmashtami
festivals.description: Birth of Lord Krishna. Fast until midnight, decorate the jhula/altar, and celebrate the birth at Nishita (midnight) with Krishna Aarti and kirtan.

festivals.name: Aja Ekadashi
festivals.description: Ekadashi vrat: fast from grains, rice and beans; worship Lord Vishnu, offer Tulsi leaves, and chant the Hare Krishna Mahamantra. Break the fast (Parana) after sunrise the next day.

festivals.name: Ravi Pradosh Vrat
festivals.description: Pradosh vrat: fast during the day and worship Lord Shiva during Pradosh Kaal, the twilight period just after sunset. Offer bilva leaves and chant Om Namah Shivaya.

festivals.name: Masik Shivaratri
festivals.description: Masik Shivaratri: monthly night of Shiva. Fast, perform abhishek on the Shivling with water or milk, and keep vigil chanting Om Namah Shivaya at midnight.

festivals.name: Bhadrapada Amavasya
festivals.description: New moon day. Take a holy bath, remember and make offerings for your ancestors (pitru tarpan), light a diya in the evening, and chant the Gayatri Mantra.

festivals.name: Hartalika Teej
festivals.description: Hartalika Teej: women observe a strict nirjala fast and worship Shiva and Parvati (Hartalika) for marital bliss, keeping vigil through the night.

festivals.name: Ganesh Chaturthi
festivals.description: Welcome Lord Ganesha home. Install the murti, offer modak and durva grass, and perform aarti morning and evening through the ten-day utsav.

festivals.name: Rishi Panchami
festivals.description: Honor the Sapta Rishis. Observe purity, offer prayers to the seven sages, and recite the Guru Brahma shloka.

festivals.name: Skanda Sashti
festivals.description: Skanda Sashti: Shukla Sashti of Lord Kartikeya (Murugan). Fast and worship Skanda for courage and victory over obstacles.

festivals.name: Balarama Jayanti
festivals.description: Appearance day of Lord Balarama, elder brother of Krishna. Worship for strength and family wellbeing.

festivals.name: Masik Durgashtami
festivals.description: Masik Durgashtami: monthly Shukla Ashtami of Goddess Durga. Fast, recite Durga Chalisa and Devi Kavach, and offer red flowers to the Goddess.

festivals.name: Radha Ashtami
festivals.description: Appearance day of Shrimati Radharani. Sing Madhurashtakam and celebrate the divine love of Radha-Krishna.

festivals.name: Parsva Ekadashi
festivals.description: Ekadashi vrat: fast from grains, rice and beans; worship Lord Vishnu, offer Tulsi leaves, and chant the Hare Krishna Mahamantra. Break the fast (Parana) after sunrise the next day.

festivals.name: Onam
festivals.description: Kerala's harvest festival welcoming King Mahabali, blessed by Lord Vamana. Lay pookalam, prepare Onam sadya, and celebrate with family.

festivals.name: Soma Pradosh Vrat
festivals.description: Pradosh vrat: fast during the day and worship Lord Shiva during Pradosh Kaal, the twilight period just after sunset. Offer bilva leaves and chant Om Namah Shivaya.

festivals.name: Anant Chaturdashi (Ganesh Visarjan)
festivals.description: Final day of Ganesh utsav — Ganpati visarjan. Perform the last aarti and bid farewell: Ganpati Bappa Morya, Pudhchya Varshi Lavkar Ya!

festivals.name: Bhadrapada Purnima
festivals.description: Full moon day. Take a holy bath, observe the Purnima vrat if you can, worship Lord Vishnu and Goddess Lakshmi in the evening, and offer prayers under the full moon.

festivals.name: Pitru Paksha Begins
festivals.description: The fortnight of the ancestors begins. Perform shraddha and tarpan, feed the needy, and remember your forefathers daily until Sarva Pitru Amavasya.

festivals.name: Vishwakarma Puja (Kanya Sankranti)
festivals.description: Worship of Vishwakarma, the divine architect. Clean and worship your tools, instruments and vehicles.

festivals.name: Vighnaraja Sankashti
festivals.description: Sankashti Chaturthi: fast from sunrise, worship Lord Ganesha in the evening, and break the fast after sighting the moon. Offer modak and durva grass.

festivals.name: Kalashtami
festivals.description: Kalashtami: Krishna Ashtami of Kala Bhairava, the fierce guardian form of Shiva. Worship at night with a mustard-oil diya and chant Om Namah Shivaya.

festivals.name: Indira Ekadashi
festivals.description: Ekadashi vrat: fast from grains, rice and beans; worship Lord Vishnu, offer Tulsi leaves, and chant the Hare Krishna Mahamantra. Break the fast (Parana) after sunrise the next day.

festivals.name: Soma Pradosh Vrat
festivals.description: Pradosh vrat: fast during the day and worship Lord Shiva during Pradosh Kaal, the twilight period just after sunset. Offer bilva leaves and chant Om Namah Shivaya.

festivals.name: Masik Shivaratri
festivals.description: Masik Shivaratri: monthly night of Shiva. Fast, perform abhishek on the Shivling with water or milk, and keep vigil chanting Om Namah Shivaya at midnight.

festivals.name: Sarva Pitru Amavasya (Ashwina)
festivals.description: Sarva Pitru Amavasya — the last day of Pitru Paksha. Perform shraddha/tarpan for all ancestors, feed brahmins, cows, crows and the needy.

festivals.name: Sharad Navratri
festivals.description: Nine nights of Goddess Durga begin with Ghatasthapana. Recite Durga Chalisa and Devi Kavach daily, join garba/dandiya, and fast if you can.

festivals.name: Kapardisha Chaturthi
festivals.description: Vinayaka Chaturthi: Shukla-paksha chaturthi of Lord Ganesha. Fast till midday, worship Ganesha at noon (Madhyahna), and offer modak and durva grass.

festivals.name: Skanda Sashti
festivals.description: Skanda Sashti: Shukla Sashti of Lord Kartikeya (Murugan). Fast and worship Skanda for courage and victory over obstacles.

festivals.name: Durga Ashtami
festivals.description: Maha Ashtami. Perform Kanya Pujan, recite Mahishasura Mardini and Devi Kavach, and offer special prasad to the Goddess.

festivals.name: Saraswati Puja (Navratri)
festivals.description: Navratri worship of Goddess Saraswati. Place books and instruments at her altar and recite Saraswati Vandana.

festivals.name: Maha Navami
festivals.description: The ninth night of Navratri — worship Goddess Siddhidatri, perform Kanya Pujan and havan, and conclude the Navratri vrat.

festivals.name: Dussehra (Vijayadashami)
festivals.description: Victory of good over evil — Rama over Ravana, Durga over Mahishasura. Perform Shami/Aparajita puja and start new ventures.

festivals.name: Papankusha Ekadashi
festivals.description: Ekadashi vrat: fast from grains, rice and beans; worship Lord Vishnu, offer Tulsi leaves, and chant the Hare Krishna Mahamantra. Break the fast (Parana) after sunrise the next day.

festivals.name: Bhauma Pradosh Vrat
festivals.description: Pradosh vrat: fast during the day and worship Lord Shiva during Pradosh Kaal, the twilight period just after sunset. Offer bilva leaves and chant Om Namah Shivaya.

festivals.name: Sharad Purnima (Kojagara Puja)
festivals.description: The moon shines with all sixteen kalas. Keep kheer under moonlight overnight and offer it as prasad; worship Goddess Lakshmi who roams asking 'Ko jagarti?' — who is awake?

festivals.name: Ashwina Purnima
festivals.description: Full moon day. Take a holy bath, observe the Purnima vrat if you can, worship Lord Vishnu and Goddess Lakshmi in the evening, and offer prayers under the full moon.

festivals.name: Karwa Chauth
festivals.description: Married women fast from sunrise to moonrise for their husband's long life, breaking the fast after offering arghya to the moon.

festivals.name: Tula Sankranti
festivals.description: The Sun enters a new rashi. An auspicious day for a holy bath, surya arghya at sunrise, japa, and charity.

festivals.name: Vakratunda Sankashti
festivals.description: Sankashti Chaturthi: fast from sunrise, worship Lord Ganesha in the evening, and break the fast after sighting the moon. Offer modak and durva grass.

festivals.name: Ahoi Ashtami
festivals.description: Mothers fast from dawn until star-sighting for the wellbeing of their children and worship Ahoi Mata.

festivals.name: Kalashtami
festivals.description: Kalashtami: Krishna Ashtami of Kala Bhairava, the fierce guardian form of Shiva. Worship at night with a mustard-oil diya and chant Om Namah Shivaya.

festivals.description: Ekadashi vrat: fast from grains, rice and beans; worship Lord Vishnu, offer Tulsi leaves, and chant the Hare Krishna Mahamantra. Break the fast (Parana) after sunrise the next day.

festivals.name: Govatsa Dwadashi
festivals.description: Worship of the cow and calf (Nandini vrat). Offer them food and gratitude before Diwali begins.

festivals.name: Budha Pradosh Vrat
festivals.description: Pradosh vrat: fast during the day and worship Lord Shiva during Pradosh Kaal, the twilight period just after sunset. Offer bilva leaves and chant Om Namah Shivaya.

festivals.name: Dhanteras
festivals.description: Diwali begins. Worship Lord Dhanvantari and Goddess Lakshmi, buy gold/silver or new utensils, and light the first diya.

festivals.name: Kali Chaudas
festivals.description: Worship Maha Kali to destroy inner negativity; light a diya facing south in the evening.

festivals.name: Masik Shivaratri
festivals.description: Masik Shivaratri: monthly night of Shiva. Fast, perform abhishek on the Shivling with water or milk, and keep vigil chanting Om Namah Shivaya at midnight.

festivals.name: Narak Chaturdashi (Choti Diwali)
festivals.description: Krishna's victory over Narakasura. Take an early oil bath (abhyanga snan), light diyas, and prepare for Lakshmi Puja tomorrow.

festivals.name: Diwali (Lakshmi Puja)
festivals.description: Festival of lights on Kartika Amavasya. Clean and decorate the home with diyas and rangoli, and perform Lakshmi Puja during Pradosh Kaal in the evening.

festivals.name: Govardhan Puja
festivals.description: Worship Govardhan hill and Lord Krishna with Annakut — an offering of many food items. Sing Govinda Namalu.

festivals.name: Bhai Dooj
festivals.description: Sisters apply tilak on brothers' foreheads and pray for their long life; brothers give gifts and a promise of protection.

festivals.name: Labh Chaturthi
festivals.description: Vinayaka Chaturthi: Shukla-paksha chaturthi of Lord Ganesha. Fast till midday, worship Ganesha at noon (Madhyahna), and offer modak and durva grass.

festivals.name: Chhath Puja
festivals.description: Offer arghya to the setting and rising Sun standing in water. A rigorous 36-hour nirjala vrat for family wellbeing.

festivals.name: Soora Samharam
festivals.description: Skanda Sashti: Shukla Sashti of Lord Kartikeya (Murugan). Fast and worship Skanda for courage and victory over obstacles.

festivals.name: Masik Durgashtami
festivals.description: Masik Durgashtami: monthly Shukla Ashtami of Goddess Durga. Fast, recite Durga Chalisa and Devi Kavach, and offer red flowers to the Goddess.

festivals.name: Kansa Vadh
festivals.description: Krishna's victory over the tyrant Kansa. Celebrated with processions in Braj; remember that dharma always prevails.

festivals.name: Devutthana Ekadashi
festivals.description: Ekadashi vrat: fast from grains, rice and beans; worship Lord Vishnu, offer Tulsi leaves, and chant the Hare Krishna Mahamantra. Break the fast (Parana) after sunrise the next day.

festivals.name: Tulasi Vivah
festivals.description: Ceremonial marriage of Tulasi Devi with Lord Vishnu (Shaligram) — the start of the wedding season. Decorate the Tulsi plant and perform the vivah puja.

festivals.name: Kartika Purnima
festivals.description: Kartika Purnima — Dev Deepawali. Light diyas by a river or at home in the evening, take a holy bath, and worship Lord Shiva and Lord Vishnu.

festivals.name: Ganadhipa Sankashti
festivals.description: Sankashti Chaturthi: fast from sunrise, worship Lord Ganesha in the evening, and break the fast after sighting the moon. Offer modak and durva grass.

festivals.name: Kalabhairav Jayanti
festivals.description: Appearance day of Kala Bhairava, the fierce form of Shiva and lord of time. Worship at night with mustard-oil diyas.

festivals.description: The day Lord Krishna spoke the Bhagavad Gita at Kurukshetra. Read a chapter of the Gita and reflect on its teaching.

festivals.name: Dattatreya Jayanti
festivals.description: Birth anniversary of Lord Dattatreya — Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva combined as the Adi Guru. Recite the Guru Brahma shloka.
